chunks: And by this chain, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'ammar ibn Khallad, who said:

A Persian man asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), saying: 'Is obeying you obligatory?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' He (the man) said: 'Like obedience to Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَن: Kunya (honorific teknonymy) of Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (AS), the eighth Imam
key_terms.طَاعَة: Obedience, compliance with the commands of an authority — in Shia theology, obedience to the Imam is a religious obligation
key_terms.مُفْتَرَضَة: Obligatory, imposed (from fard — a religious duty), indicating it is not optional but divinely mandated

ai.seo_question: Is obedience to the Imam obligatory in Shia Islam according to al-Kafi?
ai.summary: A Persian man directly asks Imam al-Ridha (peace be upon him) whether obedience to him is obligatory, and the Imam confirms it is, equating it explicitly with obedience to Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). This hadith is significant because it establishes the doctrinal continuity of the Imamate — each Imam possesses the same authority and deserves the same level of obedience as the first Imam Ali. The Persian questioner's background may reflect the influence of Persian converts who were among the earliest and most devoted followers of the Imams.
